entries.title: Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow
entries.tagline: Three coupled ODEs that proved chaos lives inside determinism.

dna.title: Lorenz Attractor — Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow
dna.core_algorithm: A reduction of Saltzman's atmospheric convection equations to three coupled nonlinear ODEs in (x, y, z). Despite full determinism, trajectories starting from infinitesimally close initial conditions diverge exponentially — the canonical demonstration of sensitive dependence on initial conditions, popularly summarized as the butterfly effect. The kernel integrates the system with a small time step and emits the trajectory as time series.

parameters.name: steps
parameters.description: Number of integration steps to plot

entries.title: Mathematical Games — The fantastic combinations of John Conway's new solitaire game 'life'
entries.tagline: Two birth/survival rules. From them: gliders, oscillators, Turing-completeness.

dna.title: Conway's Game of Life — Population Dynamics
dna.core_algorithm: A two-dimensional cellular automaton on a toroidal grid. Each cell is alive or dead; on every tick a cell survives if it has 2 or 3 live neighbors, a dead cell becomes alive if it has exactly 3 live neighbors, and otherwise it dies. From this minimal local rule, complex global structures emerge — gliders, oscillators, and Turing-complete configurations. The kernel seeds a random grid and reports the live-cell population per generation.

entries.title: A Quantitative Description of Membrane Current and its Application to Conduction and Excitation in Nerve
entries.tagline: A four-variable ODE that earned a Nobel — and still defines computational neuroscience.

dna.title: Hodgkin–Huxley Membrane Action Potential
dna.core_algorithm: A conductance-based model of the squid giant axon membrane. Voltage V evolves under capacitive, sodium, potassium, and leak currents; the sodium and potassium conductances depend on three gating variables m, h, n that themselves evolve under voltage-dependent rate constants. Injecting current above threshold produces the characteristic fast-rising / slow-recovering action potential spike train.
equations: C_m \frac{dV}{dt} = I_{inj} - g_{Na} m^3 h (V - E_{Na}) - g_K n^4 (V - E_K) - g_L (V - E_L)

entries.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
entries.tagline: Adaptive moment estimation — the default optimizer powering most of modern deep learning.

dna.title: Adam vs Vanilla Gradient Descent on the Rosenbrock Function
dna.core_algorithm: Adam tracks per-parameter exponential moving averages of the gradient (first moment) and its square (second moment), bias-corrects them, and steps with a learning rate scaled by the inverse square root of the second moment. The kernel runs Adam alongside vanilla gradient descent on the Rosenbrock banana function and emits both loss curves so you can watch Adam follow the curved valley while plain SGD oscillates.

entries.title: Computer 'Experiments' on Classical Fluids. I. Thermodynamical Properties of Lennard-Jones Molecules
entries.tagline: The symplectic integrator that conserves energy when Euler quietly explodes.

dna.title: Velocity-Verlet vs Forward Euler — Energy Conservation
dna.core_algorithm: Velocity-Verlet is a second-order symplectic integrator: it advances position using current velocity and acceleration, then advances velocity using the average of old and new accelerations. On Hamiltonian systems it preserves a shadow Hamiltonian very close to the true one, so total energy oscillates around its initial value rather than drifting. The kernel integrates a unit-mass harmonic oscillator under both Verlet and forward Euler and emits each method's total mechanical energy so you can watch Euler bleed energy and Verlet stay stable.
equations: x_{n+1} = x_n + v_n \Delta t + \tfrac{1}{2} a_n \Delta t^2

entries.title: The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis
entries.tagline: Diffusion + autocatalysis = stripes, spots, and spirals out of a uniform soup.

dna.title: Gray–Scott Reaction-Diffusion (Turing-Style Morphogenesis)
dna.core_algorithm: Two chemicals U and V diffuse and react on a 2D grid: U is consumed by an autocatalytic step that produces V, while V decays back to nothing. With suitable feed and kill rates, the homogeneous steady state is unstable to spatial perturbations — small seeds grow into stable spot, stripe, or spiral patterns. The kernel runs the Gray-Scott PDE on a torus and emits the spatial variance of V over time as a single morphogenesis curve.
equations: \partial_t U = D_u \nabla^2 U - U V^2 + F (1 - U)
\partial_t V = D_v \nabla^2 V + U V^2 - (F + k) V

entries.title: Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities
entries.tagline: An associative memory whose recall is gradient descent on a Lyapunov energy.

dna.title: Hopfield Network — Energy Descent During Associative Recall
dna.core_algorithm: Stores P binary patterns in a symmetric weight matrix via a Hebbian outer-product rule. Asynchronous sign-updates on a noisy probe state monotonically decrease a quadratic Lyapunov energy, so the dynamics flow into the nearest stored pattern. The kernel records the energy and the overlap with the target pattern over time — the energy must decrease monotonically and the overlap should approach 1 as recall completes.

entries.title: Simple mathematical models with very complicated dynamics
entries.tagline: One parameter r, one quadratic map, and the entire route from order to chaos.

dna.title: Logistic Map — The Period-Doubling Route to Chaos
dna.core_algorithm: The map x_{n+1} = r x_n (1 - x_n) is the simplest dynamical system that exhibits the full period-doubling cascade. As r increases past about 3, fixed points become 2-cycles, 4-cycles, 8-cycles, ... at decreasing intervals, accumulating at the Feigenbaum point (~3.5699) beyond which the dynamics become chaotic with windows of order. The kernel iterates the map past a transient and emits the long-term trajectory.

entries.title: Diffusion-Limited Aggregation, a Kinetic Critical Phenomenon
entries.tagline: Random walkers stick on contact — and out grows a fractal of dimension ≈ 1.71.

dna.title: Diffusion-Limited Aggregation — Fractal Cluster Growth
dna.core_algorithm: Seed a cluster with one occupied cell at the origin. Spawn a particle on a circle just beyond the current cluster radius, let it random-walk on the lattice, and stick it permanently the first time it touches a neighbor of the cluster. Repeating this grows a branching, screened, scale-invariant cluster whose radius scales as a power of the particle count — the canonical kinetic-critical fractal.

entries.title: Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems
entries.tagline: Evolution as optimization — selection, crossover, mutation on a real-valued genome.

dna.title: Genetic Algorithm — Climbing a Multimodal Fitness Landscape
dna.core_algorithm: A population of real-valued chromosomes is scored on a multimodal fitness function (sum of three Gaussian peaks). Each generation, tournament selection picks the fitter of two random parents, optional crossover blends parents, and Gaussian mutation perturbs the offspring. Over many generations the population concentrates on the highest peak — though premature convergence to a smaller peak is possible if the mutation rate or pop size is too low. The kernel emits best and mean fitness per generation.

entries.title: De analysi per aequationes numero terminorum infinitas
entries.tagline: Quadratic convergence: every iteration roughly doubles the number of correct digits.

dna.title: Newton–Raphson — Quadratic Convergence to a Root
dna.core_algorithm: Iteratively refines a root estimate of f by stepping along the tangent: x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n). Near a simple root the error squares each iteration — quadratic convergence — so reasonable initial guesses reach machine precision in roughly log_2(precision/error_0) steps. The kernel solves f(x) = x^2 - target = 0 (a square-root finder) and emits both the absolute error and its log_10 so the curvature of convergence is visible.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Number to extract square root of

entries.title: Théorie analytique de la chaleur
entries.tagline: Any periodic function is a sum of sines — and the proof launched modern analysis.

dna.title: Fourier Series — Square Wave Reconstruction
dna.core_algorithm: The square wave is the limit of an infinite sum of odd-harmonic sines: 4/pi times sum over k of sin((2k-1)x)/(2k-1). The kernel evaluates the partial sum with N harmonics over two periods and emits both the partial-sum approximation and the true square-wave target, so the user can watch Gibbs overshoot near the discontinuities and see the L2 error shrink as N grows.

parameters.name: harmonics
parameters.description: Number of odd harmonics in the partial sum
